trust_decision.summary: The proxy route decides whether a client-supplied URL may be fetched server-side by resolving the hostname once and calling ip.isPrivate on that address. The later fetch follows redirects and resolves DNS again, so the destination that is actually connected to is never checked.

landing_point.why: The summary names an insufficient fix for the /api/proxy internal-host check, and this isPrivate call is the only private-IP check in src.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /api/proxy (moved to POST /webapi/proxy, fix.diff:57-81); the body is the URL
client-side API_ENDPOINTS.proxy, used by src/utils/toolManifest.ts:10 and src/services/upload.ts:96

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route. Other server-side fetches of user URLs (chat endpoint override, plugin gateway) are documented features with their own sinks, and a solver can dismiss them as not part of the proxy.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The proxy must still fetch public URLs, such as plugin manifests and remote files, and return their bodies. A fix that refuses all redirects or all non-allowlisted hosts would break plugin manifest import and URL upload.

O6_input_shapes: redirect from a public host to a private IP (fetch follows redirects without re-checking)
hostname that resolves to a private IP at fetch time (DNS rebinding, or names like 127.0.0.1.nip.io); the agent checks at socket connect

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second server route (for example, an upload-from-URL or image-fetch webapi handler) that fetches a client URL with the old lookup+isPrivate pattern or with no filter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The client already sends remote file URLs to the proxy for upload, so a maintainer could plausibly have added a dedicated server-side fetch for that feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A local manifest-fetch helper in the gateway route that fetches manifest URLs with a hand-written isPrivate check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gateway already destructures the client-supplied manifest and indexUrl, so in-repo manifest fetching would be a natural refactor away from the external package.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918): private-address filter bypass through redirect or a TOCTOU DNS check

O10_build.project_tests: None for the proxy route at the pinned commit or in the fix. The test script is at package.json:60. Hidden tests need a local HTTP redirector and a stub resolver.

j.j_sites_touched: src/app/api/proxy/route.ts (deleted) -> src/app/webapi/proxy/route.ts; src/services/_url.ts; package.json; src/server/routers/lambda/user.ts and src/services/user/client.ts (unrelated PWA threshold)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Pass redirect:'manual' to fetch, or re-check isPrivate on each redirect hop. Either still leaves the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU between dns.lookup and the connect.

out_of_scope_notes: The chat routes use a client-supplied endpoint as the LLM SDK baseURL (src/app/api/chat/agentRuntime.ts:35, 45, 63, 95, 102, 110). The JWT carrying it is signed with a public constant (src/const/auth.ts:12), so this is a separate SSRF-style sink, not pursued.
The plugin gateway passes a client-supplied manifest/indexUrl to @lobehub/chat-plugins-gateway (src/app/api/plugin/gateway/route.ts:63-73). This is a third-party sink, not pursued.
The fix also changes an unrelated canEnablePWAGuide threshold (fix.diff:90-91, 122-123).
unverified: Whether node-fetch v3 reuses the agent from ssrfAgent(url) on redirect hops was not verified in node_modules.
Recall risk is estimated: this is the second advisory on the same route and has public write-ups.
No latest release was provided, so latest-code presence was not checked.
